page.layout: One column of running text, with one marginal note in the left margin beside the paragraph "Hæc sunt". Running head at the top right, page number at the top left. Catchword "Sup-" at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Primo gradu frigida sunt: Hordeum, Milium.
Sicca in primo gradu: Faba, Fœnum græcum, Fœniculi, Hordeum, &c.
Secundo: Ervum, Lens, Oryza, Papaveris, Solani, &c.
Tertio: Anethi, Apii, Ammi, Anisum, Careum, Cyminum, Coriandrum, Granum tinctorium, Nigella, Milium, Petroselinum, &c.
Hæc sunt Seminum qualitates Secunda. semina alterantia qualitate prima; Sequuntur quæ secunda.
Hæc vel astringunt; ut Antheæ seu antorae, Berberorum, Bursæ pastoris, Granum tinctorium, Milium, Portulacæ, &c.
Discutiunt: Anethi, Dauci, Fœnum græcum, Nigellæ, Sesami, &c.
Abstergunt: Faba, Ervum, Hordeum, Lupini, Urticæ, &c.

page.notes: The running head and page number are read from the scan. The word in the first line of the left margin note is read as "Seminum". Doubtful readings: "antorae" and "Antheæ" in the astringent list, which I could not read with certainty. The "Sup-" at the foot is a catchword.
